name: Jethro
title: Midianite priest and Moses' father-in-law
summary: Jethro (also known as Jetro/Reuel) was a Midianite priest and the father of Zipporah, who became Moses' wife. He gave Moses important advice on organizing the judicial system in Israel and acknowledged the Lord's greatness after hearing about the exodus from Egypt. He is an important figure showing God's work also outside the people of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Moses flees to Midian and meets Jethro's family
keyEvents.description: After killing an Egyptian, Moses fled to Midian, where he helped Jethro's daughters at the well. Jethro welcomed Moses and gave him his daughter Zipporah as a wife.

keyEvents.title: Jethro sends Moses back to Egypt
keyEvents.description: Moses asked Jethro for permission to return to Egypt to check on his brothers, and Jethro let him go in peace.

keyEvents.title: Jethro brings Zipporah and his sons to Moses
keyEvents.description: After the exodus from Egypt, Jethro brought Moses' wife Zipporah and his two sons Gershom and Eliezer back to Moses in the wilderness at the mountain of God.

keyEvents.title: Jethro acknowledges the greatness of the Lord
keyEvents.description: When Jethro heard about all that God had done for Israel, he praised the Lord and declared that the Lord is greater than all gods. He offered burnt offerings and sacrifices to God.

keyEvents.title: Jethro's advice on the judicial system
keyEvents.description: Jethro observed that Moses judged the people alone from morning until evening, and gave him wise counsel to appoint capable men as judges over groups of a thousand, a hundred, fifty, and ten, so that Moses would only need to handle the most difficult cases.

keyEvents.title: Jethro returns home to Midian
keyEvents.description: After giving his advice, Jethro took leave of Moses and returned to his own land.
